description: A risk committee chair must decide whether to authorize a cash tender offer for part of the company's outstanding bonds and finalize the maximum purchase amount, offer price, timetable, and control package, with input from covenant risk, legal, treasury, and investor relations.

shared_context.S1: The company has proposed a cash tender offer for up to $10,000,000 principal amount of its outstanding bonds.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary offer price is 100.0% of principal.
shared_context.S3: The company currently has sufficient reported cash to fund the proposed tender, subject to its normal liquidity controls.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding authorization decision.
shared_context.S5: Under the committee's normal deal-readiness process, covenant risk, legal, treasury, and investor relations each give a verbal clearance before Maya records the final terms.
shared_context.S6: The standard authorization form has required fields for a covenant leverage-test commitment, a tender-timetable commitment, and a two-business-day settlement commitment; each clearance owner states the applicable final value and records any required field during the scheduled clearance round before Maya decides.

PF1.text: While reconciling the latest leverage model this morning, Jonas confirmed that the tender must have a documented pro forma leverage test and that the repurchase amount must be no more than $8,000,000 to remain within the bond covenant; the result has not yet been added to the committee paper.

PF2.text: Elena received the bond-document review memo today confirming that the offer must remain open for at least 10 business days and settle exactly 2 business days after expiration; she has not yet circulated the memo to the transaction team.

PF3.text: Ravi's cash forecast, completed this morning after a large supplier payment was confirmed, was modeled at the required 101.5% offer price and includes the premium and transaction-expense budget. It shows that the company must retain a $5,000,000 liquidity floor and that the approved maximum principal tendered must be exactly $6,500,000; the forecast is not yet in the approval workbook.

PF4.text: Claire confirmed in investor calls this week that two institutional holders representing $4,000,000 principal will tender only if the price is exactly 101.5% of principal; their condition is recorded in her call notes but has not been sent to the deal team.

acceptance_conditions: The tender offer must be authorized.
The maximum principal amount tendered must be exactly $6,500,000.
The offer price must be exactly 101.5% of principal.
The offer must remain open for exactly 10 business days.
Settlement must occur exactly 2 business days after expiration.
A pro forma leverage test must be documented.
The settlement must include commitments for covenant testing, the 10-day offer period, and the 2-day settlement.
The covenant risk finding must be cited as a basis for the authorization.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ('covenant_leverage_test_commitment', 'covenant leverage-test commitment', 'covenant_leverage_test') for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ('tender_timetable_commitment', 'tender timetable commitment', 'tender_timetable') for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ('two_business_day_settlement_commitment', 'two-business-day settlement commitment', 'two_business_day_settlement', 'settlement_commitment') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The reported cash position does not establish covenant compliance; PF1 changes the settlement from an undocumented leverage assumption to a required documented pro forma leverage test and supplies the covenant basis that must be cited.

The preliminary tender terms contain no binding timetable; PF2 changes offer_open_business_days to exactly 10, settlement_days_after_expiration to exactly 2, and requires the tender-timetable and two-day-settlement commitments.

Reported cash appears to support the proposed $10,000,000 tender, but PF3 changes maximum_principal_tendered_usd to exactly $6,500,000 to preserve the $5,000,000 liquidity floor after accounting for the exact 101.5% offer price and transaction expenses.
The preliminary price is 100.0%, while PF4 changes offer_price_percent_of_principal to exactly 101.5% to secure the identified $4,000,000 of institutional participation.
